sub_answers.text: Rick DeMont was stripped of his 1972 Olympic 400‑metre freestyle gold medal after testing positive for ephedrine from his prescription asthma medication [d11321867s0p0]. The positive test also prevented him from competing in other events at the 1972 Olympics, including the 1,500‑metre freestyle, for which he was the then-current world record-holder [d36836906s4p0]. The United States Olympic Committee recognized his gold medal performance in 2001, but the International Olympic Committee had not restored the medal as of 2017 [d36836906s4p0].

sub_answers.text: She won gold in the 50-metre freestyle and contributed to gold medals in the 4×100-metre freestyle relay and 4×100-metre medley relay at the 2005 World Aquatics Championships [d901542s4p0]. She recorded a then fourth-fastest-ever 200-metre freestyle lead-off split (1:57.06) in the 4×200-metre freestyle relay final at the same championships [d901542s4p0]. She lowered the 100-metre short course freestyle world record to 51.70 at the Australian Short Course Championships in 2005 and set a short-course 200-metre freestyle world record of 1:53.29 on 19 November 2005 [d901542s4p0]. She regained the long-course 100-metre freestyle world record with a time of 52.88 on 27 March 2008 at the Australian Olympic Trials [d901542s4p0].

sub_answers.text: FINA rules require that a foot of the second, third or fourth swimmer must be contacting the platform while (and before) the incoming teammate is touching the wall, and the starting swimmer may already be in motion which saves about 0.6–1.0 seconds compared to a regular start [d182796s1p0]. Relay teams commonly record aggregate relay times that are typically 2–3 seconds faster than the sum of individual best times, reflecting faster takeovers and team-related performance gains [d182796s1p0]. Many swimmers perform better in a relay than in an individual race owing to a team spirit atmosphere, which can contribute to improved takeover timing and overall split improvements [d182796s1p0].

sub_answers.text: Trickett's 100-metre freestyle split times at the 2005 World Aquatics Championships were faster than the individual 100-metre freestyle gold medallist and world record holder Jodie Henry, which earned her the honour of swimming in the final of the medley relay at the July 2005 championships [d901542s4p0]. sub_answers.text: At the 2005 World Aquatics Championships in Montreal (July 2005) Trickett won the 50-metre freestyle in 24.59 and took silver in the 100-metre butterfly in 57.37 [d901542s4p0]. At the same championships she was part of gold-medal winning 4×100-metre freestyle (3:37.22) and 4×100-metre medley (3:57.47) relay teams, and a silver-medal 4×200-metre freestyle relay (7:54.00) team [d901542s4p0]. As lead-off swimmer in the final of the 4×200-metre freestyle relay she recorded a 1:57.06 split, which was the then fourth fastest 200-metre freestyle time in history (2005) [d901542s4p0]. Trickett lowered the 100-metre short course freestyle world record to 51.70 on consecutive nights at the Australian Short Course Championships in 2005 and set a short-course 200-metre freestyle world record of 1:53.29 on 19 November 2005 at the Sydney stop of the 2005 FINA World Cup series [d901542s4p0]. She regained the long-course 100-metre freestyle world record with a time of 53.42 on 31 January 2006 at the Australian Championships and again improved it to 52.88 on 27 March 2008 at the Australian Olympic Trials [d901542s4p0].
